title: Speed, honestly
summary: Play the hard bar at five tempos from slow to fast, and write down exactly what happens at each.
materials: the piece from your teacher, with a pencil

figure.alt: Five boxes stacked, one for each of five tempos tested in order from slow to a little faster than the target, the honest tempo table this step builds.

steps.title: Speed, honestly
steps.body:
It is tempting to test speed by jumping straight to the fastest tempo and hoping. This week tests it properly: five tempos, evenly spaced, with an honest note of exactly where things start to fall apart.

1. Pick five tempos spread evenly from your slow, safe speed up to a little faster than the piece's target.
2. Play the hard bar once at each tempo, in order, slowest first, with no retries at any single tempo.
3. Write down, honestly, the exact tempo where the first real mistake showed up.
4. Practise at the tempo just below that one, slowly building it back up, then test the same five tempos again next sitting.

A data table beats a feeling. It tells you exactly which tempo to trust and exactly which one is still asking for trouble.

figure.alt: The same five boxes, tested again each sitting, the exact tempo where the first real mistake shows up written down honestly every time.

steps.title: Four sittings
steps.body: Fifteen minutes each. Tick a sitting when it is done. Days do not matter; sittings do.
checklist: Sitting 1: play the five tempos in order, write down where the first mistake was
Sitting 2: practise just below that tempo, then test all five again
Sitting 3: practise the same way, test all five a third time
Sitting 4: the whole piece at your new safe fastest tempo, then as if recording
An old piece played once, at whatever speed feels natural

steps.title: Record this week's version
steps.prompt: Say the five tempos and where the first mistake showed up, then play the hard bar at the safest fast tempo, hands in the frame.
